Canary /search p95 is 60 ms, so the regression sits entirely above p95: roughly the slowest ~7 of 729 canary /search requests, i.e. ~1% of /search and well under 1% of total traffic. /browse (p99 30 ms) and /checkout (p99 105 ms) show no tail inflation.

1. A tail-only regression with zero errors, no p95 change and no drift over time is the weakest grade of bad-canary signal: nothing is failing, a thin slice of searches is slow.
2. The p99 comparison is structurally unfair here - canary p99 comes from ONE pod (729 /search samples) while stable p99 is smoothed across THREE pods (2273 samples). A single pod's GC pause, JIT/cache warmup or noisy-neighbour contention lands directly in its p99 and is invisible in a 3-pod aggregate.
